about: The desk bot's archive. Every fact the Askme.bot window may state lives here and nowhere else: the page answers from it when no model is connected, and the Cloudflare Worker in workers/healer/ puts the same entries in front of Claude. `entries` serve the healing path (written from the Wavesbychin site and this portfolio); `hiring` serves the recruiter path (written from this portfolio's About me, résumé, Client Work and Lab windows). Change a fact here, not in either reader. The `answer` and `ask` fields are in Vivien's first person, since both personas speak as her; `facts` stay in the third person for the model.

entries.facts: Wavesbychin is Vivi's sound healing practice in East London: sound baths, reiki, cacao ceremony and breathwork, offered live and in person. Its line is 'Somewhere to put the noise down.' Instruments: gong, Himalayan and crystal singing bowls, chimes and voice. The belief underneath it: stillness is something we can return to, not something we have to chase. The site is aibotvivi.github.io/wavesbychin-site; Instagram @wavesbychin.
entries.answer: Wavesbychin is my place to put the noise down: live sound in East London, with gong, singing bowls, chimes and voice, woven with reiki, cacao and breath. It began as my own way home to stillness, something you return to rather than chase.
entries.ask: What noise would you set down first, if the room asked nothing of you?

entries.facts: The path began with loss. When Vivi's grandmother passed away, she travelled to Nepal on her own, and that journey led her into sound healing, and into reiki as a way of understanding her own healing. The practice kept growing from there: cacao ceremony, then BaZi, which has quietly reshaped how she sees herself and the people she works with.
entries.answer: My path opened through grief. After my grandmother passed, I travelled alone to Nepal, and the bowls found me there; reiki followed as a way to understand my own healing.
entries.ask: Has a loss ever turned out to be a doorway for you, too?

entries.facts: Timeline: Feb 2023, certified in Sound Healing in Nepal. Feb 2024, certified in Reiki Level 2 in London. Dec 2025, certified in cacao ceremony facilitation by a Brazilian instructor. 2026, ongoing: studying BaZi (Chinese four-pillars astrology) and Pranic healing. The portfolio also says she trained in sound healing in Nepal and now hosts events in London.
entries.answer: The thread runs like this: I certified in sound healing in Nepal (2023), Reiki Level 2 in London (2024), and cacao ceremony with a Brazilian teacher (2025). Right now I'm still a student of BaZi and Pranic healing; the learning hasn't closed.
entries.ask: Which of those threads are you most curious to pull on?

entries.facts: Instruments are played live: gong, Himalayan and crystal bowls, chimes, voice. You lie on a mat under a blanket and listen; there is nothing to learn beforehand and nothing to perform. Most sessions begin with settling in, some breathwork or a short grounding moment, then sound with Tibetan singing bowls. Vivi works close, moving the bowls near your body so the vibration is felt as well as heard; ask for more distance and she'll adjust. Some people fall asleep. First-timers are the majority most weeks. 'You're not being asked to believe anything. You're being asked to lie down and listen.'
entries.answer: You lie down, stay warm, and the room does the rest. Bowls, gong and voice are played live and brought close, so the sound is felt in the body as much as heard, and there is nothing to believe and nothing to perform.
entries.ask: When did you last let yourself be held by a sound rather than fill the silence?

entries.facts: Close, intentional sound: primarily Tibetan singing bowls, brought close so the frequency is felt, not only heard. Shaped around you: no two sessions look the same; depending on the group, the time and the intention she draws from affirmation, chanting, breathwork, meditation, reiki, cacao and tea sharing. You can ask for specific elements such as reiki, chanting or breathwork.
entries.answer: Nothing I do follows a fixed script. I bring the bowls close, and around them I weave what the moment asks for: breath, chanting, affirmation, reiki, cacao, a shared cup of tea.
entries.ask: If you could choose one element to be woven into your hour, which would it be?

entries.facts: Group sound bath: 60 minutes, £25 per person; doors open fifteen minutes early, then an hour of sound, silence, and tea if the venue allows. 1:1 sound healing: 60 minutes, from £80 at a studio or £120 at your home; a short conversation first, then bowls on and around the body. Corporate: 45 to 90 minutes, up to 20 people, from £300, £150 for each extra session the same day. Ceremony and private events (weddings, namings, memorials, milestone birthdays, retreat closings): by arrangement, from £400. Prices are starting points; travel is quoted on top, based on distance from East London. No VAT. Sessions are rescheduled rather than cancelled. Bring your own mat, cushion or blanket and wear loose clothes.
entries.answer: A group sound bath with me is £25; a private hour is from £80 at a studio or £120 in your own home; teams start from £300, and ceremonies from £400. Each is the same instruments, held differently, and I quote travel from East London on top.
entries.ask: Are you drawn to a shared room, or to sound that is shaped for you alone?

entries.facts: Moon Phase Rituals: eight sessions across one lunar month, each shaped by where the light is. New Moon (setting down: low gong, long silences). Waxing Crescent (first movement: bowls only, light and quick, 45 min). First Quarter (friction: two instruments at odds, resolved slowly). Waxing Gibbous (tending: voice leads). Full Moon (full room: every instrument, ninety minutes, often sells out, booking opens ten days ahead). Waning Gibbous (telling: a short reading, then an hour of quiet, twelve people at most). Last Quarter (putting down: descending tones, one bowl left to fade). Waning Crescent (rest: a dawn session, forty minutes, no framing).
entries.answer: My rituals follow the month rather than the calendar: eight sessions from dark to dark, each tuned to where the light is. The New Moon is for setting something down in silence; the Full Moon fills the room with every instrument for ninety minutes.
entries.ask: Where do you feel you are in your own cycle right now: beginning, full, or letting go?

entries.facts: Corporate wellness sessions: offsites, wellness weeks, team days, launch weeks, or an ordinary Thursday afternoon. 45 to 90 minutes; needs only floor space and a door that closes. A brief framing of what sound is and isn't, the session, then space for questions. From £300 for up to 20 people. Vivi travels to your office or venue; travel is quoted before you book. Enquiries through the Wavesbychin site's message form.
entries.answer: I bring sound to teams too: 45 to 90 minutes, needing only floor space and a door that closes, from £300 for up to twenty people. I begin with an honest word on what sound is and isn't, then the quiet.
entries.ask: What would change in your team if everyone lay down together for an hour?

entries.topic: Innerwave: tarot, I Ching and dreams
entries.facts: Innerwave (InnerWaves) is Wavesbychin's companion project for tarot and dream reading, open whether or not you ever come to a session. It covers tarot spreads, I Ching hexagrams, angel numbers and dream reflection, in English and Traditional Chinese. Readings are anchored to the source imagery: reference knowledge for each drawn card or hexagram comes from a library of 78 cards, 64 hexagrams and 10 angel numbers, so readings are grounded rather than improvised. Well-rated readings become examples for future ones. It is still in progress, not publicly launched. Vivi's own view: the cards are a prompt, not a prophecy.
entries.answer: Innerwave is my companion to the sound: tarot, I Ching, angel numbers and dreams, read against a library of 78 cards and 64 hexagrams so each reading stays rooted in the old imagery. The cards, to me, are a prompt, not a prophecy.
entries.ask: Is there a question you've been carrying that you'd rather be asked than answered?

entries.topic: Who sound healing is not for, and what it is not
entries.facts: Sessions are live sound and rest, a wellness practice, not medical or mental-health treatment; they make no health claims and don't replace a doctor or therapist. Sound healing is not suitable if you're pregnant, have epilepsy or a seizure condition, have a pacemaker, metal implants or recent surgery, or have tinnitus or sound sensitivity. If unsure, ask Vivi or your doctor before booking.
entries.answer: What I offer is live sound and rest, never medicine; I make no health claims, and I walk beside your doctor or therapist rather than in place of one. Sound healing isn't suitable in pregnancy, with epilepsy, a pacemaker or metal implants, recent surgery, or tinnitus and sound sensitivity.
entries.ask: Would it help to write to me first, so I can shape the room around what your body needs?

entries.facts: Afterwards: drink plenty of water. Feeling sleepy or floaty is normal: the body has shifted into rest, so sit a moment, feel your feet on the floor, have a light snack, plan a quiet evening. Feeling emotional is normal too; let it pass without judgement, and reach out to a friend or professional if something difficult stays. If you didn't feel much, effects can be subtle or arrive later, often as deeper sleep or a calmer next day. Go easy on alcohol, strong caffeine, heavy meals and screens. Wait 10 to 15 minutes before driving.
entries.answer: Afterwards the body often stays in rest mode, so sleepy, floaty or tender are all welcome visitors. Drink water, feel your feet on the floor, keep the evening soft; and if you felt little, the sound sometimes arrives later, as deeper sleep.
entries.ask: How do you usually treat yourself after something has moved you?

entries.topic: The singing bowls on this desk
entries.facts: This portfolio has a Singing Bowls window: seven bowls synthesised in the browser, one per chakra, root to crown, C through B (root C 261.6 Hz up to crown B 493.9 Hz), the mapping sound practitioners use. A Himalayan bowl beaten by hand is never exactly in tune, which is the point of the wobble.
entries.answer: There are seven of my bowls on this very desk, one for each chakra from root to crown, C rising to B, struck in your browser. A hand-beaten bowl is never perfectly in tune; the wobble is the medicine.
entries.ask: Would you like to strike one and notice where it lands in you?

hiring.facts: Vivien Chin is a Senior Product Designer in London at JP Morgan & Chase (payments, since August 2022), currently on Fraud, Trust and Safety (2026 to present). Her line: she designs trust and safety in payments, and she builds what she designs. Her work spans fintech, enterprise and AI. Before design she spent five years in digital advertising in London and Hong Kong, which is where the client-facing half of the job was learned. Accessibility and inclusive design are the parts she will argue about.

Across the payments portfolio she has worked on initiatives including KYB onboarding, Ring Project, SEPA checkout, SmartPay and Pay by Bank enhancements.

hiring.facts: In-Car Payments (JP Morgan & Chase, Mobility Payments Solution, 2022 to 2025): a white-label wallet on wheels so drivers and passengers pay securely from the car's operating system, across mobile, tablet and infotainment. Scenarios included device binding, wallet management, functions on demand, quick-service restaurants, EV charging and parking. She ran workshops and user research and built design systems using Google Automotive OS components, working with a product lead, product manager, full-stack developers, legal and QA. The demo app was for OEM brand partners.
hiring.answer: In-Car Payments was a white-label wallet that lets drivers pay for charging, parking, food and car features from the dashboard. I led the workshops and research and built the design system on Google Automotive OS components; the full case study is in Client Work.

Users averaged 40 to 60 years old on smaller phones, so she increased font sizes, weighed button sizes and prioritised key features to reduce cognitive load.
